Tomato___healthy.explanation: Leaves exhibit normal green coloration with active chlorophyll and no signs of bacterial or fungal lesions.
Tomato___healthy.recommended_action: Maintain routine balanced irrigation, balanced N-P-K fertigation, and regular scouting.

Tomato___Early_blight.explanation: Fungal pathogen characterized by concentric target-like brown spots surrounded by yellow chlorotic halos on older lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.recommended_action: Remove and destroy affected lower foliage. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation. Apply ICAR-approved bio-fungicides (Trichoderma harzianum) or Mancozeb as per agricultural officer guidelines.

Tomato___Late_blight.explanation: Severe fungal-like oomycete infection thriving under high humidity and cool temperatures. Water-soaked dark lesions spreading rapidly across leaves and stems.
Tomato___Late_blight.recommended_action: Urgent intervention required. Destroy infected plant debris immediately. Improve air circulation. Spray copper oxychloride (0.25%) or metalaxyl upon professional confirmation.

Potato___healthy.explanation: Normal vegetative leaf canopy showing uniform green pigmentation and robust leaf architecture.
Potato___healthy.recommended_action: Continue earthing-up and preventive scouting. Maintain optimal soil moisture for tuber bulking.

Potato___Early_blight.explanation: Brown angular spots with concentric rings appearing on older leaves, often exacerbated by nitrogen deficiency and drought stress.
Potato___Early_blight.recommended_action: Apply balanced potassium and nitrogen fertilizers. Treat with approved protectant fungicides at first sign of circular lesions.

Potato___Late_blight.explanation: Devastating foliar disease causing pale green to brown water-soaked lesions with white mildew growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.recommended_action: Halt overhead irrigation immediately. Spray systemic fungicide (e.g. cymoxanil or metalaxyl-mancozeb). Monitor nearby potato/tomato fields.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.explanation: Vibrant green parallel-veined leaves showing healthy photosynthetic activity with no rust pustules.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.recommended_action: Ensure adequate nitrogen side-dressing during knee-high to tasseling stages.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.explanation: Air-borne fungal disease characterized by cinnamon-brown to golden powdery pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.recommended_action: Plant rust-resistant hybrid cultivars. If pustule coverage exceeds 10% on ear leaf before silking, apply recommended triazole or strobilurin fungicide.
